subject.title: Remote skill bin probe times out when node is co-located with gateway (macOS app as node on same host)

question: For macOS app-backed nodes, should OpenClaw keep advertised `system.which`/`system.run` and make remote skill-bin probing readiness-aware, or should it suppress probes for co-located app nodes?
rationale: The code path can be fixed several ways, but the choice affects remote execution compatibility, skill availability freshness, warning noise, and operator expectations for app-backed nodes.

options.title: Readiness-Aware Probe
options.body: Delay the initial probe until the node is ready, add bounded retry/backoff, and require live macOS proof while preserving the existing node command surface.

options.title: Skip Co-Located App Probes
options.body: Suppress the local gateway/app warning case first and leave remote macOS app timing/backoff to a narrower follow-up.

options.title: Add Disable Configuration
options.body: Introduce an operator suppression knob, accepting new config surface while leaving the underlying readiness behavior mostly unchanged.

recommendation.title: Readiness-Aware Probe
recommendation.body: Delay the initial probe until the node is ready, add bounded retry/backoff, and require live macOS proof while preserving the existing node command surface.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans the remote exec policy boundary, macOS app node behavior, and gateway product contract where the history signal is strongest.
